intro: An insertion, deletion, or substitution can change a transcription. Dynamic programming finds the fewest unit-cost edits without enumerating edit sequences.
task: Find the minimum edit cost between token sequences, checking insertion, deletion, and reordering separately.
requirements: left and right are lists or tuples of at most 10000 nonempty strings; each sequence must contain at most 500 tokens for this lesson.
Return the integer Levenshtein distance using unit insertion, deletion, and substitution costs; matching tokens cost zero.
An empty sequence requires one insertion or deletion per token. Transposition is not a single edit in this contract.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Start with empty prefixes
hints.body: The first row and column are prefix lengths, not zeros.

hints.title: Use three predecessor states
hints.body: Compare insertion, deletion, and match-or-substitution costs at every cell.

explanation: Each dynamic-programming cell stores the best cost for two prefixes. Optimal edit sequences can be extended from one of three shorter prefix pairs.
Two rows are sufficient because the recurrence only uses the current row and the previous row. The runtime is O(LR), and memory can be kept linear.
